summary: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, August Boeckh, and Franz Bopp. He held posts at Realschule, Gymnasium Schneidemühl, and succeeded Bopp as comparative philology chair at Berlin in 1872.

Hermann von Schlagintweit studied at the University of Munich (~1844-1848). A researcher in history and archaeology, he held a teaching assignment at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1851-1854) and was a member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1862-1882) and Leopoldina.
Specializing in history and archaeology, Hermanus Johannes de Graaf studied at Leiden University (~1919-1926) and under Poerbatjaraka (1927-1930).

Heymann Steinthal, a scholar of linguistics and philosophy, studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under August Boeckh (~1843-1847). He served on the faculty at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1850-1899) and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872-1899).
Hideaki Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a researcher in 1995.

Hideaki Nakatani works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and computational fields. He studied under Gadjin M. Nagao at Kyoto University (1966) and Yutaka Ochihara, earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and was attested as professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.
Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Tohoku University and was attested as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University in 2020.
Hideki Kiyoshima works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi and served as a lecturer at Kindai University around 1989.

Hideki Yukawa studied at Kyoto University and Osaka University. During his career, he held academic posts at Osaka University (~1933-1939), Kyoto University (~1939-1970), Columbia University (~1949-1953), and the University of Tokyo.
Hidemasa Nagata was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1953 to 1961 and later held an academic post there from ~1976 to 1996.

Hidenaka Tanaka was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, Oxford, and Kyoto University. He held teaching posts at Tokyo, Kyoto University (1920-1946), and Kyoto Women's University (~1951-1974).
Hidenori Kitagawa was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied under Hakuju Ui. He was attested as a professor at Nagoya University from 1968 to 1969.

Hidenori S. Sakuma specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at Shitennoji University, Taisho University, and the University of Tsukuba.

Hideo Mineshima was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Yamagata High School, Taisho University, and Waseda University. He was a lecturer, associate professor, and professor at Waseda (1960-1998) and later served at Bunkyo Gakuin University.

Hideomi Yaita works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1980-1985), worked as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1986), and was attested as a lecturer at Taisho University in 1995.
Hidetaka Fukazawa specializes in religious studies. He studied at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1976-1980) and held a post at Hitotsubashi University from ~1993 to 2020.
Hideto Ono specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1964-1973) and served as an associate professor at Aichi Gakuin University (~1987-1994).

Hidetoshi Yoshizawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held several posts at Taisho University, attested as a researcher (1998), research student (2006), lecturer (2008), and chief research fellow (2017).

Hidetsugu Yagi studied at Osaka Prefectural Kitano High School and the University of Tokyo (~1906-1909). He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University (~1919-1932), Osaka University (~1932-1946), and Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1942-1944).

Hideyo Ogawa is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hiroshima University as associate professor (~1988-1997) and professor of Indian Philosophy (~1997-2019, attested 2026).
